outcome: frequency of unplanned cesarean delivery of the second twin
cohort: The study included 2624 twins who were delivered at a Level I Perinatal Center in Germany between 2000 and 2020.
finding: Chorionicity did not significantly affect neonatal outcomes for vaginally born second twins, although monochorionic twins generally showed lower biometric measurements and parameters of physiological status.
mod_finding: For second twins, monochorionic twins delivered by cesarean section had lower birth weight due to lower gestational age, but no significant difference in birth weight was found for vaginally born second twins based on chorionicity, leading to the recommendation of vaginal delivery for monochorionic twins without primary C-section indicators.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome; monochorionic second twins delivered by C-section had lower birth weight, while vaginally born second twins showed no significant difference based on chorionicity.
gest_age: Measured as an outcome; lower gestational age at birth was noted for monochorionic second twins delivered by C-section.
